# Project Cognition

## Purpose and intended use

Preserve evidence-backed project intent and give AI-assisted software work an auditable definition of done, so locally reasonable edits do not accumulate into architecture or goal drift.

### Intended users

- maintainers using AI coding agents for multi-step software work
- teams that need project-level memory, explicit invariants, and bounded completion

### Use cases

- read-only project research before deciding what to build
- cross-session carriage of project purpose, architecture, evidence, decisions, and unknowns
- evidence-bound Simple or Governed coding loops with explicit stopping conditions

### Environment

- Node.js 22.12 or newer
- DeepSeek Harness 0.1.1-rc.2 is the pinned first client runtime; protocols v1.4-v1.11 produced preserved partial, negative, or invalid official Flash evidence, and protocol v1.12 is an offline-only scorer correction with the E1 live round stopped
- portable JSON/core modules and HostEvent v1 are client-independent; non-DSH adapters are not implemented, while version-locked Claude Code Agent SDK 0.3.251 and Codex App Server stdio 0.150.0-alpha.12.2 discovery records are both HOLD

## Architecture and boundaries

### Components

- Researcher Application: certified read-only project cognition producer
- Cognition Core: canonical project state, authority/proof status, freshness, Markdown projection
- Goal Core: approved contract revisions, attempt/event fold, completion decision state machine
- Verifier Core: frozen invocation hashes and trusted session evidence evaluation
- DSH Adapter: /researcher entryways, session-log replay, human gates, hard stop/pause/complete authority
- Adapter Core: portable HostEvent v1 plus one-shot researcher.ask and persistent researcher.mode control semantics
- Evaluation Governance: blind snapshots, locks, validity gates, feedback telemetry
- Evidence Bundle Integrity: deterministic raw-byte commitment, external Ed25519 signature verification, and verdict-aware offline scoring
- Model Cost Admission: frozen provider/model/resolved DeepSeek base URL, Beijing-time blackout windows, immutable settings, absolute deadlines, and independently recomputed host receipts

### Boundaries

- JSON state is normative; PROJECT_COGNITION.md is generated and must not be edited as a second truth
- The Research Session Ledger is provisional session evidence, not canonical project truth; it cannot directly change Project Cognition or authorize execution
- Promoting a research finding requires an explicit draft cognition revision, owner review, sealing, and deterministic projection regeneration
- Research produces evidence and draft handoff but never execution authority
- Models may execute and report observations but only the host governor may choose a terminal state
- Client adapters must not weaken portable contract, verifier, project-root, or human-approval semantics
- Recorded goal terminal events must equal the decision independently derived from their preceding evidence; labels and signatures cannot replace host or worktree evidence
- Goal Contract v1 scope fields are semantic constraints, not a generic filesystem allowlist; only E1 allowed_changes currently has hard path enforcement
- Model cost admission constrains only the official E1 runner; it does not prove OS-wide egress isolation, provider billing identity, or the absence of out-of-band calls

## Ratified invariants

- **I1 [hard]** — The certified Researcher remains read-only and cannot implement or approve its own handoff. Change policy: Requires an explicit owner-approved cognition revision and a new security/runtime review.
- **I2 [hard]** — Canonical JSON is the sole project-cognition truth; Markdown is a deterministic generated projection and the Research Session Ledger is non-authoritative input. Change policy: Any replacement must preserve one normative source, tamper detection, and deterministic human projection.
- **I3 [hard]** — A model cannot unilaterally approve, weaken, or complete a Goal Contract. Change policy: Requires explicit owner ratification; adapters lacking host-side enforcement must be labeled advisory, never governed.
- **I4 [hard]** — Failed or invalid experiments remain visible and cannot be upgraded into positive product claims or rehabilitated by later experiments. Change policy: Only new valid evidence may supersede a conclusion; historical invalidity records remain immutable.
- **I5 [hard]** — A recorded goal terminal decision must equal the host reducer result derived from its preceding trusted evidence; terminal prose or labels cannot override the reducer. Change policy: Requires an explicit owner-approved cognition revision plus runtime and evidence-integrity review.
- **I6 [hard]** — Model-backed repository evaluations must not invoke the DeepSeek API on Monday through Friday during [09:00,12:00) or [14:00,18:00) Asia/Shanghai; only an explicitly run-locked local loopback model is permitted in those windows. Change policy: Requires an explicit owner-approved cognition revision plus model-cost policy, runtime, and scorer review.

## Decisions

- **D1** — Validate DSH through the E2 value gate before implementing Claude Code as the first second-client adapter. Rationale: Portable abstractions without a measured outcome would multiply integration and maintenance cost; E3 requires a second conformant adapter only after E2 passes.
- **D2** — Use Simple and Governed modes with hard attempt/no-progress limits; the system recommends and the user confirms. Rationale: Small deterministic work should stay cheap, while architecture/security/subjective work needs explicit gates.
- **D3** — Freeze both Goal Contract content and verifier registry content by canonical SHA-256. Rationale: Freezing a verifier name alone permits silent acceptance weakening under the same id.
- **D4** — Treat the Research Session Ledger and research handoffs as provisional inputs; only an owner-reviewed, sealed canonical cognition revision may change project truth. Rationale: Separating observation from ratification prevents model inference, session replay, or Markdown edits from silently changing architecture and project purpose.
- **D5** — Use the proof order Gate 0, E1, non-inferential pilot, E2, second-adapter conformance, then E3; frozen protocols are the sole source for trajectories, estimands, and thresholds. Rationale: This order first establishes integrity, then live conformance, then measurable DSH value, and only then spends on portability and causal attribution.
- **D6** — Require sealed-only, exact-next Project Cognition installation bound to the reviewed current state hash. Rationale: The bound transition rejects direct draft installation, stale reviewed base hashes, and skipped or rollback revisions. It uses best-effort rollback for in-process write failures. Doctor detects an active/stale governance lock and a missing or mismatched canonical state/projection pair; it does not enumerate all temporary/backup residue, perform crash recovery, or claim cross-file power-loss atomicity.
- **D7** — Outside the weekday API blackout windows, DeepSeek API evaluation is permitted only with deepseek-official/deepseek-v4-flash; weekends waive only the clock blackout, never the run lock, budget, explicit cost acknowledgement, or Flash-only rule. Rationale: This preserves the owner's cost boundary while allowing reproducible remote evaluation in admitted periods; local labels alone are insufficient, so local runs require the deepseek-official adapter, a frozen literal loopback base_url, generated settings with watch=false, and exact DSH resolver checks at every model-call boundary.

## Known unknowns

- **U1** — The effect size attributable to model quality versus client enforcement is unknown.
- **U2** — A complete six-track Live E1 set, successful human gate, and admissible end-to-end resume/live-offline replay equivalence have not been proven; v1.11 resumed one real session to host-owned DONE, but its frozen scorer rejected the bundle and the preregistered stop rule ended the round before the other five tracks ran.
- **U3** — Longitudinal Project Cognition value, Goal Governor value, adoption cost, and cross-client portability remain unmeasured.
- **U4** — Protocols v1.4-v1.11 reached official Flash on DSH 0.1.1-rc.2, but complete E1 conformance remains unproven and the live round is mechanically stopped under protocol v1.12 before any live argument or cost path. Claude and Codex discovery are both HOLD rather than compatibility evidence; the Codex turn attempts retained no valid event trace and their exact account usage is unknown. Repository guards also cannot prove an honest host clock/OS scheduler, OS egress control, that a loopback service does not proxy remotely, or provider billing identity.
